summary.motive: Run true QB power with no read: use the fullback to wrong-arm the unblocked edge and the pulling guard to log the Mike, handing the quarterback a designed crease in the B/C-gap.
summary.keyDefender: Unblocked Edge Defender — forced to wrong-arm into the FB kick-out
summary.whyItWorks: The unblocked edge must choose between boxing the quarterback and squeezing the run; either choice he makes has already been blocked for, and the counter fake takes the backside linebacker out of his gap.
summary.failureMode: A long-armed edge who plays the quarterback instead of the blocker — keeping outside leverage, spilling the kick-out, and forcing the keeper wide into the force corner.

beats.title: 1. No Read, No Mesh — Pure Design
beats.text: Unlike the power read, this ball is clamped from the snap. The running back sells a counter fake the other way while the quarterback opens with his eyes on the fullback’s kick, not on any defender.

beats.title: 2. The Wrong-Arm Trap
beats.text: The unblocked edge defender is put in conflict: if he boxes, the QB bounces outside; if he crashes — which he does — the fullback kicks him out and erases the edge entirely.

beats.title: 3. Puller Logs the Second Level
beats.text: The pulling left guard arrives exactly where the MIKE fills, logging him inside-out so the B/C-gap stays open. Power means someone is always blocked at the second level — here it is the puller himself.

beats.title: 4. Quarterback Falls Forward Past the Sticks
beats.text: With the edge kicked and the MIKE logged, the only defenders left are the climbing-RT-blocked safety and a trailing free safety. The keeper converts in a phone booth — Roman’s signature short-yardage answer.

relations.tell: There is no read and no extended mesh — the QB clamps the ball at the snap and the fullback kicks the first color he sees.
